full_judgment:
6. Mr. Hasmat Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the appellate Court having found that the suit was bad for defect of parties committed an error of law is not sending the same on remand, to the trial Court, to enable the plaintiffs to implead all the necessary parties in the suit. The learned Advocate submits that the lower appellate Court failed to notice that in a suit for declaration to title necessary parties are those who denied or interested to deny the title of the plaintiff and, as such, non-impleading of all the recorded tenants of the Khatian cannot defeat the suit for defect of parties. The learned, Advocate submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, committed an error of law in not complying with the requirements of Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, According to the learned Advocate, the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal. 

 11. The plaintiff as PW 1 has deposed that Alekjan sold her share to one Sultan Patwary and Aftab Patwary about 30/35 years back. No documentary evidence has been produced nor any witness was examined to show that Alekjan ever transferred her interest in the property to Sultan and Aftab. That Sultan and Aftab were the proper persons to testify as regards transfer by Alekjan in their favour but they were not impleded as parties in the suit. It is the plaintiff himself who has admitted that share of Alakjan was transferred to Sultan and Aftab and accordingly, for non-pleading them in the suit, the plaintiffs have to face the consequences. Plaintiffs have further deposed that Abdul Quadir, son of Jora Gazi died leaving one son and two daughters Ayesha and Adarunessa. Since the plaintiffs are claiming title to 'kha' schedule property by purchase from Abdul Quadir, also the said daughters of Alekjannamel vs, Ayesha and Aduranessa are very much necessary parties, PW 1 deposed that they are alive but they have not been impleaded in the suit. Non-inclusion of the aforesaid daughters in the suit is a defect which cannot be cured at this stage. The submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal has no substance inasmuch as I find that the appellate Court has reversed the material findings on which the trial Court decreed the suit. True as submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners no issue with regard to defect of party was framed. But it appears from the pleadings of the parties and the evidence on record that the parties were aware with regard to non-inclusion of certain persons in the suit I have already held that non-inclusion of certain person in suit could not be avoided by the plaintiffs at this stage as the plaintiffs were aware about the existence of those persons. The learned Subordinate Judge has correctly found that the suit suffers from defect of parties.
